comments.author: Melfely
comments.body_html:
It VERY heavily depends on the mod. Though don’t take that other guy for his word, the programming language has not changed, the difference between 3.11.x and 4.0.x depends on the cases, it’s just a new version of .Net (6 to 9) which has new features and such. It’s still C# for client plugins and typescript/javascript for the server mods. [It seems this HAS been changed to C#]

Also it heavily depends on quite a few factors. In this case better zeroing is a bepinEx plugin simply only calling things that didn’t change between SPT and Tarkov versions.

Though the steps are the same regardless, you will want dnSPY and open up the game .dll files (forgot which one exactly) for both versions (in this case 3.11.4 and 4.0.13) then compare all the called functions and such, luckily they are all the same, so a recompile works.

AI is a great tool to help you get in the door of all the compiling boiler plate, along with looking at the GitHub repo forks for his mod.

Now for his other mod, that is NOT a BepInEx plugin so it’s using a different language and system, I have looked into it and will likely be updating it just like this one, but it does a little bit more than single plugin recompile. Since it references item IDs and you will have to make sure the system still works the same. Thought it might honestly still be close to working.

Though again AI is great tool for helping with the boilerplate compiling files and structure, it’s honestly what AI is best at in coding. Though it’s important to try and UNDERSTAND it, not just use it.
